$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Amazon Bedrock (runtime playground, knowledge bases, agents, AgentCore). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py.

bedrock.runtime.title: Bedrock Runtime playground (InvokeModel / Converse, streaming)
limitations: Every model id is answered by one small local model (llama.cpp on the mesh/appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the browser provides it): quality is toy-grade. No local model running -> ModelNotReadyException, never a canned answer. Converse/ConverseStream and Claude InvokeModel support function tool use and json_schema structured output (small-model reliability); InvokeModelWithResponseStream streams the model family's own events incrementally (Claude, Nova, Titan, Llama, Mistral). Converse/Claude `document` blocks (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, HTML, Markdown, text) are really parsed and the extracted text is sent to the model (legacy .doc/.xls and scanned PDFs are rejected; s3Location sources are not supported). `image` blocks are rejected with a ValidationException unless a vision-capable local model is configured (none is served by default). cachePoint / cache_control checkpoints are accepted and reported as cacheRead/WriteInputTokens from a real in-process prefix cache (SHA-256 of the prompt prefix, 5-minute TTL, 1024-token minimum; Converse, ConverseStream and Claude InvokeModel) - it is accounting, the compute saving comes only from llama.cpp's own prompt cache. Reasoning/thinking content is rejected because no served model emits it.

Nano: there is no model until the page registers one. The Bedrock overview offers 'Enable in-browser model (WebLLM)' (needs WebGPU; loads @mlc-ai/web-llm from a CDN and downloads a small model); without it every model call returns ModelNotReadyException. The in-browser model serves the console page that loaded it, not the external SDK relay endpoint.

bedrock.knowledge-bases.title: Knowledge bases (S3 data sources, ingestion, Retrieve, RetrieveAndGenerate)
limitations: Ingestion really reads the S3 data source, chunks (fixed size / hierarchical parent-child / semantic embedding-breakpoint / none) and embeds with the local embedding seam; Retrieve is exact cosine kNN (no ANN index) with overrideSearchType HYBRID (BM25 via SQLite FTS5 fused with the vector ranking by reciprocal rank fusion, the default) or SEMANTIC (vector only; scores are cosine similarities) and the full RetrievalFilter set (equals, notEquals, greaterThan/OrEquals, lessThan/OrEquals, in, notIn, startsWith, stringContains, listContains, andAll, orAll, validated like Bedrock: one operator per filter, 2-5 members, typed values), plus implicitFilterConfiguration (the small local model derives the filter from the question; invented attributes are ignored). Reranking works on Retrieve (rerankingConfiguration, metadataConfiguration) and the bedrock-agent-runtime Rerank API (amazon.rerank-v1:0 and cohere.rerank-v3-5:0 ARNs, TEXT documents only, 1000 sources, numberOfResults): by default the reranker is NOT a cross-encoder but embedding similarity blended with query-term coverage (the response trace says 'embedding+lexical'); set VYOMI_RERANK_ENDPOINT to a Jina/Cohere/llama.cpp-style /v1/rerank server (for example llama-server --reranking with a bge-reranker GGUF) to get a real cross-encoder on the Mesh; none is shipped, and Nano always uses the embedding blend. Text, CSV, HTML, Markdown, PDF (pure-Python pypdf; scanned PDFs have no OCR), DOCX, XLSX and PPTX are parsed (legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt fail); parsingStrategy BEDROCK_FOUNDATION_MODEL keeps tables as markdown but is not a model call, BEDROCK_DATA_AUTOMATION is rejected; .metadata.json sidecars (plain and typed) feed Retrieve filters; unreadable documents are listed per file in the ingestion job's failureReasons. On Nano PDF needs pypdf to be loaded into Pyodide (otherwise PDFs fail with an explicit reason). The vector store type named at creation is recorded but the index always lives in the account (no OpenSearch/Pinecone/etc). Without an embedding model on the backend, vyomi-hash-embed (a deterministic bag-of-words embedding) is used, so retrieval is lexical-ish, not semantic. Every model id is answered by one small local model (llama.cpp on the appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the browser provides it): quality is toy-grade. No local model running -> ModelNotReadyException, never a canned answer.

bedrock.agents.title: Agents (create, prepare, aliases, knowledge bases, InvokeAgent)
limitations: Agent versions/aliases snapshot the prepared agent; InvokeAgent prompts the local model with the instruction, session history and retrieved knowledge-base passages and returns citations. Function-schema and OpenAPI (JSON, or YAML when PyYAML is available) action groups with a Lambda executor are really invoked through the Lambda engine with the Bedrock Agents event, and the result is fed back to the model; RETURN_CONTROL groups return the returnControl event and accept returnControlInvocationResults on the next InvokeAgent. Tool selection uses schema-constrained JSON output, validated against the action schema with bounded retries (after which the agent answers it is unable to assist, with a failureTrace) - a <1 GB model still chooses tools far less reliably than a production model. enableTrace emits preProcessing/orchestration/postProcessing/guardrail/failure trace parts from the real loop (pre/post-processing are deterministic steps, not model calls). guardrailConfiguration applies the guardrails engine to input and output; memoryConfiguration SESSION_SUMMARY summarises a session at endSession (memoryId) and feeds it to later sessions, with GetAgentMemory/DeleteAgentMemory (no summary on idle-timeout expiry). Not implemented: multi-agent collaboration, built-in AMAZON.UserInput/CodeInterpreter groups, apiSchema from S3, requireConfirmation prompts, custom prompt templates/parsers, enhanced (non-text) inputs. Every model id is answered by one small local model (llama.cpp on the appliance, WebLLM on Nano when the browser provides it): quality is toy-grade. No local model running -> ModelNotReadyException, never a canned answer.

bedrock.agentcore.gateway.title: AgentCore gateways and targets (MCP)
limitations: Gateways expose a real MCP JSON-RPC endpoint (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) at POST /gateways/{id}/mcp on the Vyomi wire, not at the *.gateway.bedrock-agentcore hostname. Lambda targets are really invoked. CUSTOM_JWT is really validated (RS256 signature against the JWKS of the discoveryUrl issuer - this simulator's Cognito pools in-process, any other issuer by OIDC discovery - plus issuer, expiry, allowedAudience, allowedClients, allowedScopes; 401 for bad/missing/expired tokens, 403 for audience/client/scope mismatch; RS256 only, needs `cryptography`, so it fails closed where that is unavailable). openApiSchema targets (JSON or YAML) become callable tools named <target>___<operationId> (path/query/header params and JSON body, $ref resolved) and mcpServer targets are proxied over MCP streamable HTTP; both need outbound network, so they work on the Mesh/appliance and return an isError result inside Nano's browser sandbox. API-key and OAuth2 client-credentials credential providers (CreateApiKeyCredentialProvider / CreateOauth2CredentialProvider, GetResourceApiKey / GetResourceOauth2Token M2M) feed the target's outbound auth; the OAuth USER_FEDERATION (browser consent) flow, vendor-specific discovery and workload-identity token verification are not implemented. smithyModel targets are registered but not callable; AWS_IAM gateways only check that an Authorization header is present.

bedrock.agentcore.runtime.title: AgentCore runtime (hosted agents) - Vyomi agent spec, Dev Simplified
limitations: Dev Simplified: runtimes are control-plane records (CreateAgentRuntime/Get/List/Update/Delete, versions, runtime endpoints with DEFAULT, CREATING->READY) and InvokeAgentRuntime really runs an agent - but NOT your container. A runtime whose environmentVariables carry VYOMI_AGENT_SPEC (JSON: instructions + declarative tools: static/template/builtin calculator/webhook/in-process function) is executed in-process as a tool-calling loop over the local model (llama.cpp on the mesh/appliance, WebLLM on Nano; payload {"prompt": ...}, runtimeSessionId keeps multi-turn history, Accept: text/event-stream streams steps). A container-only runtime returns RuntimeClientError (424); no model running -> 503 ServiceUnavailableException, never a canned answer. Quality is toy-grade; no container/ECR pull or InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand. Runtimes with protocolConfiguration.serverProtocol MCP (spec tools served as an MCP server: initialize, tools/list, tools/call) or A2A (JSON-RPC message/send, tasks/get, agent card; agent runs the spec over the local model) answer JSON-RPC payloads; the A2A card is served as an RPC method, not at /.well-known/agent-card.json, and there is no streaming or push notification. AgentCore Memory (events + long-term records) is hooked in through the spec's memory block; Identity covers API-key / OAuth2 credential providers only, and runtime inbound JWT is decoded, not signature-verified. Webhook tools need network egress (not available in Nano's browser); on Nano the loop re-runs after each model await, so keep tools idempotent. State is in the persisted account bag.

bedrock.guardrails.title: Guardrails (CreateGuardrail, versions, ApplyGuardrail, Converse guardrailConfig) - Dev Simplified
limitations: Dev Simplified: deterministic simple filters, not Bedrock's trained classifiers. Word lists (custom + small PROFANITY list), denied topics (name/example phrase match), regex PII (EMAIL, PHONE, US SSN, card, IP, AWS key, URL and more) with BLOCK/ANONYMIZE, custom regexes, and content filters (HATE, INSULTS, SEXUAL, VIOLENCE, MISCONDUCT, PROMPT_ATTACK) whose LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH strength is honoured against a confidence from keyword hits plus, only when a real embedding model is up, a zero-shot embedding-prototype score (conservative thresholds, not calibrated against a labelled set; without a real embedder it is keywords only). Contextual GROUNDING and RELEVANCE filters (thresholds, scores, grounding_source/query/guard_content qualifiers, Converse guardContent) are scored by word coverage plus embedding cosine: a deterministic scorer, thresholds behave the same but absolute scores differ from Bedrock's. Converse, ConverseStream, InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream check input and output; stream output is judged in ~1000-character windows (sync holds a window until judged and can mask or replace it, async streams then only reports), so a violation split across two windows can be missed. Automated reasoning, image content and cross-Region config are rejected. State is kept in the persisted space account bag and survives a restart.
